# Prior art in Postgres schema diffing

Ticket: [smonn/db#7](https://github.com/smonn/db/issues/7). Researched 2026-10-20.

**Question.** How do existing Postgres schema-diff tools introspect the catalog, model it, and order the DDL they generate? What should our diff engine reuse, and what pitfalls should it avoid?

**Our constraints** (from the ADRs in this repo): the Current migration is generated by diffing a TypeScript Definition against a Shadow database that replays the Committed migrations (ADR-0003). Kinds of object the Definition cannot express are ignored, never dropped (ADR-0005). Output is portable SQL (ADR-0002). The runtime is zero-dependency, with the diff behind a subpath export (ADR-0006). Migration files may opt out of a transaction (ADR-0008).

Evidence tags: **[src]** read in a clone of the repo at the cited commit; **[doc]** read on the project's docs site or in the PostgreSQL docs; **[sum]** came from a fetch-tool summary of a page and was not read verbatim, so treat as lower confidence. Source links pin a commit.

## Answer in brief

1. Every tool that works well avoids normalizing the "desired" side itself. They load it into a real Postgres (temp DB, shadow DB, embedded Postgres), introspect both sides with the same queries, and diff two catalog models. Atlas, pg-schema-diff, pg-delta and pgschema all do this. Our Definition should do the same.
2. Introspect `pg_catalog`, not `information_schema`. Use `pg_get_indexdef`, `pg_get_constraintdef`, `pg_get_expr`, `pg_get_viewdef` and `format_type` as the comparison form for anything that is an expression or a clause. Pin `search_path` first, or the same catalog deparses differently per connection.
3. Order the DDL with one dependency graph over atomic actions (bare `CREATE TABLE`, constraints and indexes as separate actions) and a deterministic Kahn sort. That is what pg-delta and pg-schema-diff converged on. Fixed phase lists (migra) work but need repair code for each new cycle shape.
4. No tool detects renames safely by default. Atlas moved from interactive prompts to an explicit `renamed_from` annotation. pg-delta has structural-hash detection but ships it off. Ship drop and create, flag it as data loss, and consider an explicit annotation later.
5. Handle destructive changes with typed hazards on each action, not a regex over the output (migra) and not blocking generation.
6. Our ADR-0005 rule needs one addition the tools do not have to face as sharply: an ignored object (a hand-written view or trigger) can block a modeled change (`cannot alter type of a column used by a view`). Detect that through `pg_depend` and warn. Do not drop it.

## 1. migra and schemainspect

Deprecated, but the clearest small codebase and the one our design most resembles. [src: migra 3450382, schemainspect 066262d]

**Introspection.** schemainspect runs one SQL file per kind from [`pg/sql/`](https://github.com/djrobstep/schemainspect/tree/066262d/schemainspect/pg/sql). It reads `pg_catalog` directly: `pg_class`, `pg_attribute`, `pg_attrdef`, `pg_index`, `pg_constraint`, `pg_depend`, `pg_rewrite`. It calls `pg_get_viewdef`, `pg_get_indexdef`, `pg_get_expr`, `format_type` and `pg_get_function_identity_arguments`. `information_schema` appears only for privileges (`role_table_grants`) and as type names copied into the functions query. Version differences are text templates in the SQL (`-- 12_ONLY`, `-- PRE_12`), stripped at load time ([`obj.py` L1108-1136](https://github.com/djrobstep/schemainspect/blob/066262d/schemainspect/pg/obj.py#L1108-L1136)). Extension members are excluded with a `pg_depend` join on `refclassid = 'pg_extension'::regclass` in every query, for example [`relations.sql` L1-8](https://github.com/djrobstep/schemainspect/blob/066262d/schemainspect/pg/sql/relations.sql#L1-L8).

**Model.** `PostgreSQL` inspector holds ordered dicts per kind (`tables`, `views`, `functions`, `constraints`, `indexes`, `triggers`, ...) keyed by a quoted signature such as `"public"."t"` or `"public"."f"(integer)`. Each inspected class defines `__eq__` over the fields that count. "Modified" just means not equal ([`obj.py` L1148-1165](https://github.com/djrobstep/schemainspect/blob/066262d/schemainspect/pg/obj.py#L1148-L1165)).

**Dependencies.** [`deps.sql`](https://github.com/djrobstep/schemainspect/blob/066262d/schemainspect/pg/sql/deps.sql) reads only view-to-relation and view-to-function edges, via `pg_depend` joined to `pg_rewrite` rows named `_RETURN`, `deptype = 'n'`. `load_deps` adds trigger, enum-column and inheritance edges in Python, then `load_deps_all` computes transitive `dependents_all` ([`obj.py` L1225-1290](https://github.com/djrobstep/schemainspect/blob/066262d/schemainspect/pg/obj.py#L1225-L1290)). Functions that use tables in their bodies are not tracked, because Postgres does not record them (see issue [#92](https://github.com/djrobstep/migra/issues/92)).

**Diff.** `differences()` splits two dicts into added, removed, modified, unmodified. A modified object is dropped and recreated, unless it is replaceable (a view or function with compatible columns, then `CREATE OR REPLACE`) or a table (column-level `ALTER`s). If a modified view is not replaceable, all its `dependents_all` are pulled into the modified set so they are dropped and recreated too ([`changes.py` L335-399](https://github.com/djrobstep/migra/blob/3450382/migra/changes.py#L335-L399)).

**Ordering.** Two layers.
- A fixed phase list in [`add_all_changes`](https://github.com/djrobstep/migra/blob/3450382/migra/migra.py#L87-L124): schemas, extensions, collations, enums, sequences (create); then drop triggers, RLS policies, privileges, non-PK constraints, matview indexes, non-table selectables, PK constraints, indexes; then table changes; then drop sequences, enums; then create indexes, PKs, other constraints, views, matview indexes, privileges, policies, triggers; then drop collations, schemas.
- Inside a phase, [`statements_from_differences`](https://github.com/djrobstep/migra/blob/3450382/migra/changes.py#L56-L154) loops: emit every drop with no pending dependents and every create with no uncreated dependencies, repeat, and raise `cannot resolve dependencies` if a pass makes no progress.

**Enums.** An enum whose values change is renamed to `<name>__old_version_to_be_dropped`, recreated, columns are re-cast, and the old type is dropped ([`changes.py` L157-207](https://github.com/djrobstep/migra/blob/3450382/migra/changes.py#L157-L207)). This works inside a transaction, unlike `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` before PG 12.

**Destructive handling.** [`statements.py`](https://github.com/djrobstep/migra/blob/3450382/migra/statements.py) checks every statement against the regex `drop\s+` and raises `UnsafeMigrationException` unless `--unsafe` is passed. Pitfall: this flags `alter column ... drop default` and `drop not null` too, and it knows nothing about `ALTER COLUMN TYPE` rewrites or lossy casts.

**Renames.** Not supported; a rename is a drop and an add. Issue [#29](https://github.com/djrobstep/migra/issues/29) is open.

**Known gaps** (open issues): comments ([#69](https://github.com/djrobstep/migra/issues/69)), view ownership ([#160](https://github.com/djrobstep/migra/issues/160)), function-to-table ordering ([#92](https://github.com/djrobstep/migra/issues/92)), enum-array columns ([#203](https://github.com/djrobstep/migra/issues/203)). Supabase's own post names domains, publications, comments, RLS policy alters and grants as the reasons it replaced migra [sum: [blog](https://supabase.com/blog/declarative-schemas-2-0-pg-delta)].

## 2. pg-schema-diff (Stripe)

Most polished Go implementation, and the best reference for hazards. [src: pg-schema-diff 9ada471]

**Introspection.** [`internal/queries/queries.sql`](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/internal/queries/queries.sql), compiled with sqlc. All `pg_catalog.*` and fully qualified, with no `information_schema`. Notable queries:
- [`GetIndexes` L138](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/internal/queries/queries.sql#L138): `pg_get_indexdef(c.oid)` as the definition, plus `indisvalid`, `indisprimary`, `indisunique`, the owning constraint (joined on `conindid`, `contype IN ('p','u')`) with `pg_get_constraintdef`, the parent index for partitions, and column names via `unnest(indkey) WITH ORDINALITY`.
- [`GetViews` L487](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/internal/queries/queries.sql#L487): `pg_get_viewdef(c.oid, true)` plus, per view, the tables and exact columns it depends on, from `pg_depend` joined to `pg_rewrite` (`d3.classid = 'pg_rewrite'`, `ev_class = view`). Column-level view dependencies let it know which column alters block on a view.
- [`GetDependsOnFunctions` L292](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/internal/queries/queries.sql#L292): `pg_depend` rows with `deptype = 'n'` pointing at `pg_proc`.
- Every query excludes extension members with `pg_depend ... deptype = 'e'`, and skips `pg_catalog`, `information_schema`, `pg_toast*`, `pg_temp*`.

**Desired side.** [`schema_source.go`](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/pkg/diff/schema_source.go): `DDLSchemaSource` applies the `.sql` files to a temp database, then introspects it with the same queries. `DBSchemaSource` introspects a live DB. Both give the same `schema.Schema` type. After generating a plan it applies the plan to a temp copy of the current schema and checks the result ([`plan_generator.go`](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/pkg/diff/plan_generator.go), `validatePlan` option, default on). Issue [#170](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/issues/170) asks why not `pg_dump --schema-only`, which tells you how often people ask.

**Diff.** Generic [`diffLists`](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/pkg/diff/diff.go#L87-L144): objects matched by name; present on both sides means build a per-kind diff, and the diff can declare `requiresRecreation`, which turns into a delete plus an add. Output is sorted by name for determinism. Duplicate names are an error.

**Ordering.** [`sql_graph.go`](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/pkg/diff/sql_graph.go) and [`sql_vertex_generator.go`](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/pkg/diff/sql_vertex_generator.go):
- Every object has up to two vertices: `(obj, DELETE)` and `(obj, ADDALTER)`. A vertex with no statements is a legal no-op, so dependencies can always attach.
- Each generator declares `GetAddAlterDependencies` and `GetDeleteDependencies` as edges between vertices. The documented invariant: after `(Y, DELETE)` runs, Y must be gone, even if something else cascaded the drop, so an empty-SQL delete vertex still keeps its edge.
- Topological sort is greedy with a priority: adds are `Sooner (+1)`, deletes `Later (-1)`, weighted by statement count. So index builds run before index drops and drops sink to the end unless an edge forces them earlier. [`graph.go` L140](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/internal/graph/graph.go#L140) is deterministic and returns an error on a cycle.
- Online index replacement renames the old index to a temp name, builds the new one concurrently, then drops the old.

**Hazards.** [`plan.go` L11-26](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/pkg/diff/plan.go#L11-L26) lists typed hazards: `ACQUIRES_ACCESS_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK`, `DELETES_DATA`, `HAS_UNTRACKABLE_DEPENDENCIES`, `INDEX_BUILD`, `INDEX_DROPPED`, `CORRECTNESS`, `AUTHZ_UPDATE`, and more. They attach to a `Statement` (with its own `statement_timeout` and `lock_timeout`). `DROP TABLE` and `DROP COLUMN` carry `DELETES_DATA` ([`sql_generator.go` L914-923](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/blob/9ada471/pkg/diff/sql_generator.go#L914-L923)). `apply` refuses a plan whose hazards are not allowed.

**Pitfalls it documents.**
- Renames are not detected: "If you rename an object, it will be treated as a drop and an add" (README, "Unsupported migrations").
- Dependencies of non-SQL functions cannot be tracked, so it emits `HAS_UNTRACKABLE_DEPENDENCIES` and asks the user to order by hand (issue [#129](https://github.com/stripe/pg-schema-diff/issues/129)).
- Column-order changes are ignored by default (`ignoreChangesToColOrder: true`), because Postgres cannot reorder columns.
- Supported versions in the README: 14 to 17. PG 18 is not listed.

## 3. Atlas

The open-source repo is a reduced build; most Postgres coverage lives in a proprietary binary. [src: atlas 1879644; features page via [sum]]

**What the open source contains.** Per the [features page](https://atlasgo.io/features) [sum], tables, columns, indexes, check/unique/exclusion constraints, foreign keys, enums and comments are open. Partitions, views, materialized views, functions, procedures, sequences, extensions, RLS, composite and domain types, and triggers are listed as Pro. The code matches: [`sql/internal/sqlx/sqlx.go` L683-694](https://github.com/ariga/atlas/blob/1879644/sql/internal/sqlx/sqlx.go#L683-L694) has `fixRenames`, `askForColumns` and `askForIndexes` as `// unimplemented.` stubs. So the Atlas parts that matter most to us (rename prompts, views, functions) cannot be read, only described from docs.

**Introspection.** [`sql/postgres/inspect.go` L1447-1656](https://github.com/ariga/atlas/blob/1879644/sql/postgres/inspect.go#L1447-L1656). A hybrid. Columns come from `information_schema.columns` joined to `pg_class`, `pg_attribute`, `pg_type` for `format_type` and `attnum`. Tables use `information_schema.tables` joined to `pg_class`. Indexes are pure catalog and the most structured of any tool: one row per index key from `generate_series(1, array_length(indkey,1))`, with `pg_get_indexdef(indexrelid, ord, false)` for the per-key expression, `pg_index_column_has_property(..., 'desc' | 'nulls_first' | 'nulls_last')`, opclass, `reloptions`, `indnullsnotdistinct` (PG 15+), `pg_get_expr(indpred, ...)` for the partial predicate, and INCLUDE columns. It has separate query variants below 11, above 11 and above 15. Checks use `pg_get_expr(conbin, conrelid)`.

**Model.** `schema.Realm > Schema > Table > Column / Index / ForeignKey`, with attributes as typed `Attr` lists ([`sql/schema/schema.go`](https://github.com/ariga/atlas/blob/1879644/sql/schema/schema.go)). A `Normalizer` interface converts a desired schema to its "normal form", "two schema objects are equal if their normal forms are equal" ([`sql/schema/inspect.go` L158-169](https://github.com/ariga/atlas/blob/1879644/sql/schema/inspect.go#L158-L169)). In practice that normalization is done by running the desired schema on a **dev database**. The [docs](https://atlasgo.io/concepts/dev-database) [sum] say without one "Atlas may propose incorrect or unnecessary changes". For versioned workflow: "Atlas loads the current state by replaying the migration directory onto the provided dev database" ([versioned diff doc](https://atlasgo.io/versioned/diff) [sum]). That is the same shape as our Shadow replay.

**Diff to changes.** The differ emits typed changes (`AddTable`, `DropTable`, `ModifyTable{Changes}`, `RenameTable`, `AddObject`, ...). Postgres-specific comparisons live in [`sql/postgres/diff.go`](https://github.com/ariga/atlas/blob/1879644/sql/postgres/diff.go): `defaultEqual`, `typeChanged`, `trimCast`, `identityChanged`, index attribute and opclass comparisons. That file is evidence of how much normalization is needed when you do not let Postgres do it.

**Ordering.** [`sql/internal/sqlx/plan.go`](https://github.com/ariga/atlas/blob/1879644/sql/internal/sqlx/plan.go):
1. [`DetachCycles` L98](https://github.com/ariga/atlas/blob/1879644/sql/internal/sqlx/plan.go#L98): topologically sort changes by table FK references. On a cycle, split every FK out of its `CREATE TABLE` into a later `ALTER TABLE ... ADD FOREIGN KEY`, and move FK drops before table drops.
2. [`SortChanges` L393](https://github.com/ariga/atlas/blob/1879644/sql/internal/sqlx/plan.go#L393): push drops (`DropSchema`, `DropTable`, `DropObject`) to the end by default, then build edges by asking `dependsOn(c1, c2)` for **every pair** of changes (O(n^2)), then DFS emit. A comment says the drops-last default exists "in case we miss any dependency between changes".
3. Postgres [`state.plan`](https://github.com/ariga/atlas/blob/1879644/sql/postgres/migrate.go#L67-L107) runs schema creates first (`topLevel`), then the sorted changes.
Schema drops use `DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE` ([`migrate.go` L160](https://github.com/ariga/atlas/blob/1879644/sql/postgres/migrate.go#L160)), which is a destructive shortcut we should not copy.

**Renames.** Before v0.22 a rename was drop plus add; v0.22 added a detector that "interactively asks the user" [sum: [release](https://github.com/ariga/atlas/releases/tag/v0.22.0)]. The newer changelog says "The interactive rename prompt is a human-only contract: agents cannot answer it", and adds a declarative `renamed_from` attribute (HCL) or `-- atlas:renamed_from <prev>` comment (SQL) for tables, columns and indexes, so the planner emits `ALTER ... RENAME` ([changelog](https://atlasgo.io/changelog/declarative-schema-renames) [sum]).

**Destructive and lock analysis.** Lint analyzers on the generated migration [doc/sum, [analyzers](https://atlasgo.io/lint/analyzers)]: DS101 drop schema, DS102 drop table, DS103 drop non-virtual column; MF101-MF104 data-dependent (adding a unique index, a NOT NULL column to a non-empty table); PG101-PG109 lock and concurrent-index checks (for example "Indexes cannot be created or deleted concurrently within a transaction", PG103); PG301 type change needing a rewrite. It lints the SQL after generation, a separate pass from planning.

## 4. Supabase pg-delta (and pg-topo)

The most relevant prior art: TypeScript, recent, built after its authors hit the failure modes of the older design (a ~54k-line engine with Postgres semantics re-implemented in eight places). Read in full. [src: pg-toolbelt 72e47ea]

Its own account of the rewrite: [`docs/overview.md`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/docs/overview.md), [`docs/architecture/target-architecture.md`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/docs/architecture/target-architecture.md), and the glossary in [`CONTEXT.md`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/CONTEXT.md). The package is alpha and says breaking changes can land between releases.

**Core bet.** "PostgreSQL is the only elaborator." Every input state is resolved by a real Postgres (the live DB, or a shadow DB populated from `.sql` files). The engine never parses SQL to understand it ([`overview.md` §2](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/docs/overview.md)). Static analysis (`pg-topo`, libpg-query WASM) survives only to pre-sort statements when loading the shadow, advisory only.

**Introspection.** One module per catalog family under [`src/extract/`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/tree/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/src/extract). All `pg_catalog`; `information_schema` shows up only in two incidental spots. Deparse functions used: `pg_get_indexdef`, `pg_get_constraintdef`, `pg_get_viewdef`, `pg_get_triggerdef`, `pg_get_functiondef`, `pg_get_expr`, `pg_get_partkeydef`, `pg_get_ruledef`, `format_type`. Highlights:
- Whole extraction runs in **one** `BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` transaction, with `SET LOCAL search_path TO 'pg_catalog'` ([`scope.ts` L592-601](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/src/extract/scope.ts#L592-L601)). The comment explains: `format_type` and every `pg_get_*def` "path-relativizes names, so anything visible on the session `search_path` comes back UNQUALIFIED. Pinning to `pg_catalog` forces every non-catalog reference to be schema-qualified, so the SAME catalog hashes identically regardless of the database's / role's / connection's default path." PostgreSQL's own tools do the same: `ALWAYS_SECURE_SEARCH_PATH_SQL` is `SELECT pg_catalog.set_config('search_path', '', false);` ([`common/connect.h`](https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/master/src/include/common/connect.h)).
- The `pg_depend` resolver is [set-based](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/src/extract/dependencies.ts#L77-L95) and keeps `deptype IN ('n', 'a')`. They profiled extraction and found this one query was 86% of the time; rewriting it from a correlated subquery to a hash join made extraction 4.2x faster ([`overview.md` §6](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/docs/overview.md)).
- `pg_get_*def` can fail with `cache lookup failed` under concurrent DDL, because it reads the latest catalog, not the transaction snapshot. They retry on a fresh snapshot, up to three times ([CHANGELOG alpha.54](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/CHANGELOG.md), entry `0d88e30`). Not a concern for us: we only introspect private databases.

**Model.** A flat `FactBase`: `Map<StableId, Fact>` where each `Fact` is `{ id, parent?, payload, hash }`. Table, column, default, constraint, index, trigger, policy, comment and ACL are each their own fact, so a diff can say "the default of `column:public.users.email` changed" with no per-type diff code. Identity is a typed, name-based `StableId`, never an OID; the identity string codec exists once ([`target-architecture.md` §3.1](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/docs/architecture/target-architecture.md#L134-L225)). Dependency edges are data (`pg_depend`-derived plus ownership and extension membership). Payloads hold canonical `pg_get_*def` strings. Facts are content-hashed with Merkle rollups so diffing is O(changed); that is an optimization aimed at 12k-object databases and is not something we need.

**Diff and rules.** A generic differ emits `add | remove | set | link | unlink` deltas ([§3.3](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/docs/architecture/target-architecture.md#L292-L319)). A per-kind **rule table** is the only kind-specific code: for each changed attribute, either an in-place `ALTER` or `replace: true` (drop and create), plus declared lock class, rewrite risk and data-loss class ([§3.4](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/docs/architecture/target-architecture.md#L321-L375)).

**Ordering.** ([§3.5-3.6](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/docs/architecture/target-architecture.md#L377-L428), [`plan/graph.ts`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/src/plan/graph.ts))
- Actions are atomic and about 1:1 with deltas: bare `CREATE TABLE`, then each constraint, default, FK, index, grant and comment as its own action. Each action declares what it `produces`, `consumes`, `destroys`.
- Edges: from the old state's edges for teardown ("an action destroying X follows everything that consumes X"), from the new state's edges for build, plus identity conflicts (remove `X` before adding a new `X`).
- One heap-based Kahn pass with tie-break by kind weight, then canonical identity. A cycle throws with the full path and is treated as a bug in a rule. "pg_dump has no cycle-breaker module because at this granularity, cycles structurally cannot form."
- A final optional **compaction** pass folds adjacent actions into idiomatic compound DDL (constraints inlined into `CREATE TABLE`) when no edge crosses the merge.
- The old engine had three hand-written cycle breakers, each added after a field-discovered cycle, and its own normalization fought them. That is the cautionary tale for phase lists plus repair.

**Renames.** [`plan/renames.ts`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/src/plan/renames.ts): over the remove/add pairs, find facts whose identity-free structural hash matches (same content, different name). Modes `auto | prompt | off`, **default off**. "Never guess": ambiguous matches (n x m equal hashes) are surfaced, not applied. Honest limit in the header: payloads that mention other objects by name break the match, so those degrade to drop and create. Supabase's blog says the CLI does not detect renames and flags the drop for manual rewrite [sum].

**Safety.** Per-action metadata (lock class, rewrite risk, data-loss class) rolls up into a hazard report: `data_loss`, `rewrite_risk`, `non_transactional`, `access_exclusive_lock`, plus coverage diagnostics ([`plan/hazards.ts`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/src/plan/hazards.ts)). The **proof loop** applies the plan to a throwaway clone, re-extracts, and asserts zero drift and that seeded rows survived ([§3.7](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/docs/architecture/target-architecture.md#L430-L485)). Data-preservation matters because a `DROP TABLE` plus `CREATE TABLE` converges to an identical schema and destroys every row.

**Unmodeled objects.** This is ADR-0005's problem and they solved it in a way worth copying. [`extract/unmodeled.ts`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/src/extract/unmodeled.ts) runs a provenance-aware completeness scan in the same snapshot and emits one `unmodeled_kind` warning per kind of user object it does not model (casts, operators, text search, statistics, transforms, ...). Built-in and extension-owned objects are excluded. `--strict-coverage` turns warnings into a hard stop. Unmodeled objects produce no facts, so they can never enter a plan. A related `unmodeled_drift` warning fires when the shadow has an unmodeled object the target lacks and a generated statement would depend on it. Coverage is listed in [`COVERAGE.md`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/COVERAGE.md).

**Pitfalls it found** (from [`CHANGELOG.md`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/CHANGELOG.md), all fixed in the last ~10 alphas):
- **Deparsed text is not a fixed point.** Postgres keeps some expressions nested (`b BETWEEN 0 AND 10 AND a >= 0`) but flattens them when it reads its own output back, "so the stored text depends on how many times an object was parsed". This rebuilt triggers, views, check constraints, indexes, policies and defaults on every sync (entry `7f2fd64`, issue #510). Their fix replays both sides' text in the shadow "until each stops changing" and compares those results.
- **PG 18 stores NOT NULL as a `pg_constraint` row** (`contype = 'n'`; domains since PG 17). Resolving it as a constraint produced dangling edges (entry `1476a72`, [`dependencies.ts` L22-37](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/src/extract/dependencies.ts#L22-L37)). They keep NOT NULL as a column attribute.
- **Postgres silently drops an inline `UNIQUE`** whose columns equal a PRIMARY KEY or another UNIQUE in the same `CREATE TABLE`, so compaction must leave those as `ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT` (entry `c03c015`).
- **Cycles through function dependencies on a dropped table** (an index expression or CHECK that calls a function taking the table's row type) needed explicit "drop index, then function, then table" ordering (entry `b325cec`).
- **Extension-owned data was dropped** by the old engine (pg_partman partitions, pgmq queues) because it saw rows the desired state lacked. Now `managedBy` edges filter them (`overview.md` §1).
- **Retyping a partition key column** must replace the partitioned table (alpha.56).

## 5. Graphile Migrate

Not a differ, but the origin of ADR-0003, so the relevant facts are about the Shadow database. [src: migrate 2cfadbb]

- Dev uses two databases. The shadow DB is "used internally by `graphile-migrate` to test the consistency of the migrations and perform various other tasks". Production uses only the main DB ([README](https://github.com/graphile/migrate#setup)).
- `reset` runs `DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS` then `CREATE DATABASE` and replays all committed migrations ([`commands/reset.ts` L38-45](https://github.com/graphile/migrate/blob/2cfadbb/src/commands/reset.ts#L38-L45)). `commit` runs the current migration against the shadow to validate it.
- It diffs nothing. It recommends dumping the shadow with `pg_dump` into a tracked file so reviewers see the schema delta, and warns that "all members of your team should run the same PostgreSQL version to ensure that the shadow dump matches for everyone".
- Roles are managed outside migrations because they are cluster-wide. Our Shadow database inherits the same constraint (see pitfalls).
- `--! no-transaction` is the same escape hatch as our `transaction:false` in ADR-0008.

## 6. pgschema and Drizzle, briefly

**pgschema** ([README](https://github.com/pgplex/pgschema), [`internal/diff`](https://github.com/pgplex/pgschema/tree/24c6b68/internal/diff)). Declarative Postgres-only tool by Bytebase. Its README states it "uses an embedded Postgres instance internally" for the desired state, which is the same "run it on a real engine" answer. Its catalog queries use `pg_get_expr` (23 call sites), `pg_get_constraintdef`, `pg_get_indexdef`, `pg_get_viewdef`, `pg_get_triggerdef`, `pg_get_function_sqlbody`. Ordering is per-kind topological sorts (tables by FK, views by dependency, functions by body references) rather than one graph. That is the older, more fragile pattern that pg-delta's rewrite argues against. No rename detection found in `internal/diff`.

**drizzle-kit** (the model ADR-0003 rejected). Compares a JSON snapshot of the current schema against the previous snapshot and prompts for renames ("prompt developer for renames if necessary") [sum: [docs](https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/drizzle-kit-generate)]. This is the design ADR-0003 chose against; nothing here changes that.

---

## 7. Cross-cutting findings

### Catalog versus information_schema

Use `pg_catalog`. Reasons, in order of weight:
1. `information_schema` is a SQL-standard view layer. PostgreSQL's docs say it "do[es] not, however, contain information about PostgreSQL-specific features; to inquire about those you need to query the system catalogs" ([information schema](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/information-schema.html) [doc]). Indexes, partial predicates, opclasses, enum labels, partitions, RLS policies, triggers' deparsed definitions and `pg_depend` are catalog-only.
2. It hides what the current role cannot access. For example, "Only those columns are shown that the current user has access to (by way of being the owner or having some privilege)" ([`columns`](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/infoschema-columns.html) [doc]). A Shadow connection owns everything, so this is survivable for us, but it is one more reason to avoid it.
3. Only Atlas leans on it (columns, tables), and it still joins back to `pg_class` and `pg_attribute` for `attnum` and `format_type`. migra, pg-schema-diff, pg-delta and pgschema do not.

### Deparse functions

The PostgreSQL docs call each of `pg_get_indexdef`, `pg_get_constraintdef`, `pg_get_viewdef`, `pg_get_triggerdef` and `pg_get_functiondef` "a decompiled reconstruction, not the original text of the command". `pretty = true` "suppresses unnecessary parentheses and adds whitespace for legibility", but "the default format is more likely to be interpreted the same way by future versions of PostgreSQL; so avoid using pretty-printed output for dump purposes" ([functions-info](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-info.html) [doc]). So: use the default (non-pretty) form for anything we compare or emit. pg-schema-diff passes `pretty = true` for `pg_get_viewdef`, which is a choice for readability that we should not copy for comparison. Two further rules from the tools above: pin `search_path`, and treat deparsed text as comparable only when both sides came through the same Postgres major version.

What each tool takes structured and what it takes as a deparsed string:

| Kind | Structured from catalog | Deparsed string used for equality |
|---|---|---|
| Column | name, `attnotnull`, `attidentity`, `attgenerated`, `format_type(atttypid, atttypmod)`, collation | default via `pg_get_expr(adbin, adrelid)` |
| Index | `indisunique`, `indisprimary`, `indisvalid`, access method, `reloptions` | `pg_get_indexdef(oid)` (migra, pg-schema-diff, pg-delta) or per-key `pg_get_indexdef(oid, n, false)` (Atlas) |
| Constraint | type, columns | `pg_get_constraintdef(oid)`, includes `NOT VALID` and referential actions |
| View | dependencies | `pg_get_viewdef(oid)` |
| Function | identity args via `pg_get_function_identity_arguments` | `pg_get_functiondef(oid)` |

### The pg_depend facts we need

From the [`pg_depend` docs](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/catalog-pg-depend.html) [doc]: `n` normal, `a` auto (dropped with the referenced object even without CASCADE), `i` internal (the part of an owning object, for example a view's ON SELECT rule), `e` extension member, `x` auto-extension, `P`/`S` partition. "Most objects created during `initdb` are pinned", so no rows exist for dependencies on built-ins. pg_depend does not see inside function bodies written as strings, which is why migra, pg-schema-diff and pg-delta all have a gap or a hazard for function-to-table ordering (the fetch tool said this from general knowledge; the docs page itself did not cover it [sum]). Edges used by tools: migra `n` via `pg_rewrite` only; pg-schema-diff `n` and `e`; pg-delta `n` and `a`, plus `i` for identity-column sequences (ownership is a separate `owner` edge, not a `pg_depend` row).

### How the desired side is normalized

| Tool | Method |
|---|---|
| pg-schema-diff | Apply DDL to a temp DB, introspect |
| Atlas | Dev database, with a Go-side `Normalizer` for the rest |
| pg-delta | Shadow DB from `.sql` files, then replay deparsed text to a fixed point |
| pgschema | Embedded Postgres |
| drizzle-kit | None; snapshot JSON, so no ground truth |

### Destructive-change handling, compared

| Tool | When | How |
|---|---|---|
| migra | After generation | Regex `drop\s+` over all statements; false positives and false negatives |
| pg-schema-diff | During generation | Typed hazards per statement; apply must allow-list them |
| Atlas | After generation | Lint analyzers on SQL (DS10x, MF10x, PG10x/PG30x) |
| pg-delta | During planning | Per-action safety metadata; hazard kinds; policy in the caller; proof checks data survives |

---

## 8. Recommendations for our diff engine

Ordered by how much they shape the design. Each says why and what we skip.

**R1. Materialize the Definition and introspect it like the Shadow.**
Render the Definition to DDL, apply it to a scratch database (a second throwaway DB, or a schema inside one), and introspect both sides with the same queries into the same model. Do not write a TypeScript normalizer that predicts what Postgres will store.
- Why: four independent tools made this choice, Atlas's docs say skipping it yields "incorrect or unnecessary changes", and Atlas's `diff.go` (`defaultEqual`, `trimCast`, type-alias handling) shows the cost of the alternative.
- Cost: a second database per generate run. Coordinate with the PGlite research ticket: an in-process Postgres makes this cheap.
- Name: GLOSSARY.md defines "Shadow database" as the replay of Committed migrations. The scratch DB holding the Definition needs its own term. Needs a domain-modeling pass; do not reuse "Shadow".

**R2. One introspection module, `pg_catalog` only, one snapshot, pinned `search_path`.**
- Open `BEGIN ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` and `SET LOCAL search_path TO pg_catalog` per extraction ([`scope.ts` L592](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/src/extract/scope.ts#L592-L601)).
- Query per kind, not one mega-query. Start from pg-schema-diff's `GetIndexes` and `GetViews` (MIT), pg-delta's dependency resolver (PostgreSQL License), and Atlas's per-key index query (Apache-2.0) for opclass, ordering and `nulls` handling. All three licenses permit copying with notice; do not paste without attribution.
- Exclude: `pg_catalog`, `information_schema`, `pg_toast*`, `pg_temp*`, and extension members via `pg_depend ... deptype = 'e'`.
- Key identities by name (schema, table, column, function identity args), never by OID. OIDs differ between the two databases.
- Pick a supported range (pg-delta's corpus runs PG 14 to 18) and record the Postgres major version in the model. Do not parametrize SQL with text templates like migra's `-- 12_ONLY`; branch in TypeScript on `server_version_num`.
- Concurrency (`cache lookup failed` retries) does not apply: both databases are private.
- Skip for now: parallel snapshot export, statement-timeout budgets, Merkle hashing. They solve 12k-object databases; an app schema has hundreds of objects. "Why now?" has no answer.

**R3. Model: a flat map of facts, a parent link, name-based ids, edges as data.**
`Map<StableId, Fact>` where `Fact = { id, parent?, payload }`, and `edges: Array<{ from, to, kind }>` from `pg_depend`. A column default, a constraint and an index are separate facts so the differ is generic and a single changed default is one delta. Payload is plain data (strings for deparsed clauses, booleans, numbers) compared with a stable deep-equal. Keep the payload free of the fact's own name so a rename feature can be added later, but do not hash.
- Why: pg-delta's own overview credits this shape with deleting per-kind diff code and the cycle breakers.
- Avoid migra's "modified means drop and create" default for tables; it is only safe for views and functions.

**R4. Order with one graph and a deterministic Kahn sort over atomic actions.**
- Actions: bare `CREATE TABLE` (columns only), then PK, UNIQUE, CHECK, FK, indexes and defaults that cross-reference as their own actions. This is pg_dump's approach, and it means mutual-FK cycles cannot form.
- Edges: build edges from the desired model's references; teardown edges from the current model (an action that destroys X runs after every action that consumes X). An in-place change is "destroy old, produce new", so the graph orders dependent teardown and rebuild around it.
- Tie-break: kind weight, then identity. Copy migra's phase order as the kind weights so the output reads like a migration a human would write: schemas, types, sequences, tables, columns, constraints, indexes, FKs last; drops before creates only where an edge says so.
- A cycle throws with the path and is a bug in our rules. No repair subsystem.
- Size: [`graph.ts`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/src/plan/graph.ts) is about 100 lines including a min-heap. We need no dependency for it.
- Skip compaction at first; it is a cosmetic peephole pass. Add it when hand-editing the Current migration makes the verbosity hurt.

**R4a. Why a graph and not migra's phases.**
Phases are right for a small closed set of kinds and need no graph, so start there if the first Definition only has tables, columns, indexes, constraints and enums. The graph is the better first design anyway because ADR-0005 expects the Definition to grow. Migra and Atlas both show the failure mode of phases: every new cross-kind interaction (function to table, view to column) adds a special case. pg-delta's old engine had three cycle breakers for the same reason.

**R5. Make ADR-0005 safe: project to modeled kinds, but watch edges from the ignored side.**
- Project both introspected models onto the kinds the Definition can express. Everything else is invisible to the differ, so it cannot be dropped.
- Still read `pg_depend` rows from ignored objects (a hand-written view, trigger, policy, function) to modeled objects. If a planned action would drop, retype or rename something an ignored object depends on, emit a hazard naming the blocker. Do not drop and recreate the ignored object: that would contradict ADR-0005 and we do not model its definition.
  - Example: a hand-written view selects `users.email`. The Definition changes `email` from `text` to `varchar(100)`. `ALTER COLUMN TYPE` fails at apply time ("cannot alter type of a column used by a view or rule"). The hazard surfaces that when generating, not when replaying.
- Copy pg-delta's completeness scan for the "optional warning naming the version that plans to support it" in ADR-0005: one query per unmodeled kind, excluding built-ins and extension members. Their [`unmodeled.ts`](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/packages/pg-delta/src/extract/unmodeled.ts) is a good checklist of kinds.
- Function bodies are not tracked by `pg_depend`. A hand-written function that selects from a table we drop will not be flagged. Say so in the warning text and move on; pg-schema-diff's `HAS_UNTRACKABLE_DEPENDENCIES` hazard is the precedent.

**R6. Destructive changes: typed hazards from the action, emitted as comments, gated at commit.**
- Each action kind declares hazards (`data_loss`, `rewrite`, `access_exclusive_lock`, `non_transactional`) in a table, the way pg-delta's rule table and pg-schema-diff's `Statement.Hazards` do. Classify from the model (drop table, drop column, narrowing type change, `SET NOT NULL`), not from the SQL text.
- Write each hazard into the Current migration as a SQL comment above the statement (`-- hazard: data_loss`). The file stays portable SQL (ADR-0002), and a reviewer sees it in the diff.
- Do not block generation: the Current migration is regenerated on every Definition edit and applied to a dev database. Gate at `commit` instead, where the migration becomes immutable history. Open question below.
- `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` and `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` cannot run in a transaction block with other work. Emit them as a hazard `non_transactional`; `commit` can split them into a `transaction:false` file (ADR-0008). Default to plain `CREATE INDEX`; this is a dev-loop tool first.

**R7. Renames: no heuristic in v0. Offer an explicit annotation if we want them.**
- Default is drop and create, flagged `data_loss`. Every surveyed tool does this, and the two that detect renames (Atlas prompt, pg-delta structural hash) both document the failure modes: ambiguous matches, name-bearing payloads that break hash equality, and prompts that automation cannot answer.
- If renames matter, the pattern that survived is a declarative annotation in the Definition (`renamedFrom: "old_name"`), as Atlas moved to. It is reviewable, deterministic, works in CI and agents, and makes the ADR-0002 output a plain `ALTER ... RENAME`. This needs a Definition API decision and probably an ADR.
- Why not a structural-hash suggestion now: it needs the identity-free payload discipline from R3 (cheap) plus a policy surface and a prompt UX (not cheap). No ticket demands it.

**R8. Verify with an oracle, not snapshots of SQL.**
Test the engine with: build Shadow from migration set A, build the scratch DB from Definition B, generate the migration, apply it to the Shadow, re-introspect, assert zero diff against the scratch DB. Run it over a corpus of (A, B) pairs and both directions. pg-delta's old engine carried about 34k lines of per-type tests asserting SQL strings; the rewrite replaced them with a 331-scenario corpus run this way ([`overview.md` §4](https://github.com/supabase/pg-toolbelt/blob/72e47ea/docs/overview.md)). Add a seeded-row survival check for any pair that claims no data loss (pg-delta's data-preservation proof) because a drop and create converges to an identical schema.
- Also the deparse fixed-point problem (below) is only found this way.

**R9. Plan for the deparse fixed point.**
Compare `pg_get_*` text only after both sides came through the same major Postgres version. If the corpus shows spurious diffs on expression-bearing kinds (check constraints, defaults, partial index predicates, generated columns), adopt pg-delta's fix: re-apply each side's deparsed text in a rolled-back transaction until the text stops changing, then compare. Do not build that on day one; build the corpus test (R8) first so we see whether we need it.

## 9. Pitfalls checklist for the design

- Deparse functions depend on `search_path`. Pin it.
- Deparsed text is not a fixed point (pg-delta #510).
- PG 18 stores NOT NULL as `pg_constraint` `contype = 'n'`. Model NOT NULL as a column attribute and exclude `'n'` rows from constraint and dependency queries.
- An inline `UNIQUE` equal to a PK or another UNIQUE is silently dropped by `CREATE TABLE`. Emit such constraints as `ALTER TABLE`, or do not inline.
- Column order cannot change in Postgres. Ignore order differences (pg-schema-diff default), but a new column always appends.
- Generated columns, identity columns and inherited columns cannot be altered the same way as plain ones. migra drops and recreates on a generated status change; for inherited columns it special-cases.
- Extension-owned objects are everywhere (`pg_depend deptype 'e'`). Exclude them from both models, and if the Definition ever models extensions, treat their member tables as read-only.
- Sequences owned by identity or serial columns come and go with the column. pg-schema-diff skips a sequence drop when its owning table or column is dropped. Model sequence ownership or hide owned sequences.
- Roles, and anything in a cluster-wide catalog, leak out of a throwaway database. Same-cluster scratch DBs are only safe for database-local objects (pg-delta `target-architecture.md` §3.2, Graphile Migrate README). Our Shadow replay of hand-written migrations that `CREATE ROLE` will leak; document it, or run Postgres per generate run.
- Replaying with `check_function_bodies = off` is needed so function creation order is not an error (migra emits it; pg-delta turns it back on to validate afterward). A typo in a function body then reaches the Shadow unless re-validated.
- Hand-edited Current migrations (ADR-0003): none of the tools cover this. We stop regenerating once edited. The diff engine should be pure over two models so the "show the diff instead of overwriting" mode reuses it.

## 10. Open questions for the ticket owner

1. **Scratch DB name and cost.** What is the glossary term for the database that holds the materialized Definition, and does the PGlite ticket make a second in-process Postgres per run acceptable?
2. **Where does the destructive-change gate live?** My recommendation is `commit`, not generation. Needs a decision before the CLI design.
3. **Do we want renames in v1?** My recommendation is no, with `renamedFrom` as the shape if yes. That decides whether the Definition keeps old names around.
4. **Which kinds does the first Definition model?** The answer decides whether R4's graph is needed on day one or phases are enough. I recommend the graph regardless, but the tradeoff is real if the first release is tables, columns, indexes and constraints only.

## Unverified or limited

- Atlas's rename prompt, views, functions and triggers live in a proprietary binary. Everything about them here comes from docs pages read through a fetch-tool summary [sum], not source.
- The Supabase CLI default switch to pg-delta: one search summary says CLI v2.115.0 made it the default for `db diff`, the October 2026 blog says it is the declarative-schemas engine. I did not resolve which CLI version flipped what. Treat "replaced migra" as true for declarative schemas 2.0, and nothing more specific.
- No tool was run. All behavior here is from reading source at the pinned commits, changelogs and docs. I did not test any of them against PG 18.
- `pg_depend` not recording references inside string function bodies is standard Postgres behavior but the fetched docs page did not state it; it is corroborated by pg-schema-diff's `HAS_UNTRACKABLE_DEPENDENCIES` hazard text and migra issue #92.
- pg-schema-diff README lists PG 14 to 17 at the pinned commit; its issue tracker may show newer support.
- The `results` successor to migra was only checked at README level.
